name: FocalPoint
summary: In smartphone AR with the free hand reaching into the scene, a selection cylinder cast from the screen adapts to where on the screen the user tends to select, a plane attached to the hand makes everything in front see-through, and the best-scoring object snaps to the pinch.
howItWorks: The phone is held in one hand and the other hand is tracked (Leap Motion on the phone, or MediaPipe). The focal region is a circle fitted to the screen positions of the last ten selections and extruded from the screen into a cylinder; candidates within twice its radius are scored by their screen distance to the focal centre and their distance to the hand, and the best one is outlined in red. A pinch within 3 mm snaps it to the hand. An occlusion plane 3 mm behind the hand makes objects in front of it transparent and unselectable, and object opacity encodes depth. With 12 participants selecting 3 mm cubes from piles, accuracy was 70% against 24% for a direct-manipulation baseline and selection was 5.5 s faster.
